title: Claude API memory tool and context editing
by: Anthropic's API docs. Read in full: the memory tool page and a summary of the context editing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing); docs.claude.com redirects there.
summary: The memory tool (type memory_20250818, name memory) lets Claude keep files under /memories across conversations. Claude only asks for operations; the application runs them against its own storage and must block paths outside /memories. It pairs with context editing, which clears old tool results, and with compaction: memory keeps what must survive when context is cleared or summarised.
ideas: Six commands: view (directory or file, optional view_range), create, str_replace (old_str must be unique), insert (after insert_line), delete and rename (fails if the destination exists).
The API adds a fixed protocol to the system prompt: 'ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE', record progress as you go, and 'ASSUME INTERRUPTION'.
The reference return and error strings are fixed, so the model learns one contract whatever the storage behind it.
The handler owns safety: canonicalise every path, reject traversal, cap file size, expire files not read for a long time.
Context editing (clear_tool_uses_20250919 with trigger, keep, clear_at_least, exclude_tools) warns Claude before clearing so it can save to memory first, and reports what it cleared.

For multi-session work: an initializer session sets up a progress log and a feature checklist, each session starts by reading them and ends by updating them, and a feature is marked done only after end-to-end verification.

took.idea: A small fixed verb set with fixed result and error strings
Read brain before anything else, every session
Assume interruption: write the step to the intent's trace as you go
The tool validates every path and refuses anything outside brain's folders
Mark a step done only after it is verified
